confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Very narrow cone cosine cancellation and binary32 cosine collapse
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: Use squared chord 4*sin(theta/2)^2 for cone limits and flux solid angle. Require a normal binary32 interval before GPU smoothstep.

confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Derived intensity and projected source radius may exceed binary32
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: Validate finite range before conversion. GPU radiance is bounded before distance attenuation, and HDR output is saturated to finite half-float maximum.

confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Clamping distance before direction normalization distorts near-light direction
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: Use true distance and SafeDirection for light direction, clamp only inverse-square attenuation denominator.

confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Point-face selection differed from the normal-biased projection location
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: Both selection and matrix projection use the same BiasedPosition. Private HLSL-based regression reproduces old failure and verifies current fix.

confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Uniform outer-cone solid angle undercounted declared luminous flux under the actual smoothstep angular falloff
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: ComputeSpotSolidAngle integrates the unit-peak falloff as pi*(innerChordSquared+outerChordSquared)/2. VisualRuntime uses the shared result for flux-to-intensity conversion. Five independent polar-angle quadrature cases catch the old formula.

confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Clamping point-light filter taps to a single face introduces cubemap seams
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: Out-of-face taps map through the production cube projection conventions into a neighboring slice. Sampled depth is reconstructed to distance, converted into the original face axis and projected for the same reverse-depth comparison.

confirmed_findings_resolved.issue: Cross-face addressing alone retained a visible planar-receiver PCSS seam
confirmed_findings_resolved.resolution: Point-light sampling now uses a face-independent radial tangent kernel, Duff stable orthonormal basis, actual fetched texel rays, and receiver-plane intersections. Geometric derivatives are evaluated before the sky branch and light loop. This supersedes the intermediate source-face depth conversion path.

capacity_checks: FrameConstants size and offsets match C++ static_asserts and reflected HLSL exactly.
Each frame constant upload starts at aligned resource base. First draw begins at 3072, subsequent draw slots have 256-byte alignment.
Four directional plus 28 local matrix slots use (4+28)*256=8192 bytes, including the final 64-byte matrix.
Local-shadow texture has max(1,view count) slices. Six views per point and one per spot yield at most 28.
Unique cross-kind light IDs and contiguous point faces make the first ID match the base slice. Shader major-axis face is in [0,5].
At most eight light records, with float-exact counts and indices. Renderer startup validates configuration via BuildLocalShadows before GPU upload.
Current source uses two explicit ID scans, one for each kind. No separately named findShadowIndex helper was present at review time.

cross_face_review.result: Final radial sampling and receiver-plane implementation reviewed; no actionable issue identified in this code snapshot.
cross_face_review.supersedes: Intermediate cross-face readdressing tests established mapping correctness but left a visible half-plane discontinuity in the GPU stress image. That intermediate implementation was replaced.
cross_face_review.basis: Duff signed-Z orthonormal basis keeps denominator magnitude at least one and avoids the near-south-pole cancellation found in the intermediate Frisvad implementation.
cross_face_review.depth: The fetched texel center defines a cube ray. Stored face-axis depth becomes radial distance by multiplying by that ray length. Receiver comparison uses the intersection of the same texel ray with the local receiver plane.
cross_face_review.receiver_plane: Geometric normal comes from ddx/ddy of reconstructed world position before divergent sky return and local-light branches; it is normalized once. Normal-map normal remains the bias direction. The plane passes through the same biased position.
cross_face_review.filter: PCSS blocker average and kernel radius are radial and independent of the selected cube face. Positive reverse-depth bias is converted to a nonnegative radial comparison gap.
cross_face_review.layers: Each tap chooses a dominant cube face within the validated six-layer point block. Projected texels are clamped within the chosen layer. Spotlights retain the original planar PCF/PCSS route.
cross_face_review.numeric_evidence: Actual HLSLI executes through the C++ texture/intrinsic adapter. Final pole and plane cases are formal rendering tests.
